digest.intro: The Gulf is burning, the uncanny valley is gone, and Voyager hit one light-day.

items.title: Iran Strikes Kuwait and Bahrain; Gulf Conflict Enters New Phase
items.blurb: Iran launched drones at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem Air Base (hosting US forces) and triggered two Bahraini air defense alerts inside three hours — the fourth attack on Bahraini territory in six days — after US jets destroyed an IRGC missile platform on Qeshm Island. Simultaneously an ADNOC tanker took a hit in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthis struck the Saudi East-West pipeline and fired cruise missiles at Riyadh, and Saudi Arabia responded with strikes on 60 Yemeni targets. At Shenzhen APEC, Xi personally met Trump on the tarmac in a protocol-breaking embrace — hours after proclaiming Russia ties 'firm as a rock' — which is the picture that will outlast any communiqué today.

items.title: Russia's Gleiwitz Gambit: False Flag Near Kaliningrad Foiled
items.blurb: Polish intelligence, tipped by partner services, thwarted a GRU-planned operation near the Kaliningrad border designed to produce mass casualties and be pinned on Ukraine — explicitly compared by Polish sources to the 1939 Gleiwitz incident that Germany used to justify invading Poland. Russian intelligence officers coordinating sabotage crossed to the border's edge before Polish forces moved, and police were repositioned to specific pre-identified sites. If confirmed at scale, this is the most brazen hybrid-warfare provocation against NATO's eastern flank on record.

items.title: Putin Won't Negotiate; Ukraine Strikes Kerch; Brussels Proposes €45B Loan
items.blurb: Multiple sources confirm Putin remains uninterested in serious peace talks, even as Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge and Europe races to lock in support before any US-brokered carve-up. The EU's €45B loan proposal and Trump's Board of Peace report — which accused both Israel and Hamas of failing ceasefire commitments — suggest Washington is simultaneously managing two war files with diminishing credibility on both.

items.title: AI Faces Now Read as More Real Than Real Faces — and Your Brain Can't Catch It
items.blurb: In an fMRI study, participants rated AI-generated faces as more realistic than actual human faces — meaning they were performing worse than random chance, actively misled rather than merely uncertain. The key mechanism: AI faces suppress activity in the anterior insula, the region that flags untrustworthy cues, because they're statistically optimized to hit every 'human' feature without the noise of real individuality. The uncanny valley, as a protective instinct, is functionally closed.

items.title: Meta's Muse Is Leaking Strangers' Bank Balances Into Random Conversations
items.blurb: Internal Meta chats obtained by Reuters show staff testing Muse received unprompted outputs including specific Capital One and Charles Schwab balances belonging to unknown users — and in one case, Muse told a staffer that context it had pulled about a coffee table pickup 'doesn't seem to be yours.' These aren't edge-case hallucinations; they're cross-account context leaks, which is a structurally different and more alarming failure mode than confabulation.

items.title: Will Wright Wants to Simulate People You Actually Know
items.blurb: MyMems, Wright's first project since Spore, inverts the simulation: instead of generic agents, it ingests your memories to generate plausible behavioral models of your grandmother, your sister, your old coach — then puts them in puzzle scenarios together. Wright's critique of The Sims was always that 'plausible behavior' was nowhere near capturing why his sister and he fought so much, and this is the attempt to close that gap. Whether it lands as intimacy or extractive novelty is the question the demo will have to answer.

items.title: Vhils and Cidade Wrap a São Paulo Colonial Building in Emergency Blankets
items.blurb: At Rua Cardeal Arcoverde 2878 in Pinheiros, the two artists fixed survival-kit thermal blankets to a colonial facade with cornstarch glue — the material simultaneously preserving and masking the building's condition, mirroring passersby in faint silver, shifting color with daylight. The concept: a structure can disappear before demolition, losing its presence in everyday experience while its address remains. The Christo echo is obvious, but the choice of emergency material — something you wrap a person in when they might die — is the sharper decision.

items.title: Metabolism: Buildings as Living Organisms, Born From Atomic Anxiety
items.blurb: The 1960 Metabolism manifesto — by Kikutake, Kurokawa, Maki, and critic Kawazoe — wasn't just formal experimentation: it was a post-atomic identity project, trying to hold Western modernism and pre-war Japanese culture in the same frame by making buildings literally cellular and replaceable. Their conceptual DNA came from the Ise Shrine, which is ritually demolished and rebuilt every 20 years to remain both ancient and new. The movement produced floating cities and capsule towers, but its deepest argument was that cultural resilience requires designed impermanence.

items.title: Voyager 1 Is One Light-Day Away. Here It Is, Down to a Single Memory Chip.
items.blurb: Raj Shekhar built an interactive exploded-view of both Voyager spacecraft that lets you open the nuclear RTG down to its 24 individual plutonium spheres, then descend into the flight data computer to a single chip — released on the day Voyager 1 crossed one light-day from Earth. It's the kind of obsessive craft that makes the object feel real again after 49 years of abstraction: a machine launched in 1977, still transmitting, now so far that its signal takes 24 hours to arrive.

facts.fact: AI-generated faces were rated as more realistic than actual human faces by study participants, who performed worse than random chance at detection — actively misled, not merely uncertain.
A Meta staffer testing Muse received an unprompted message stating 'your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57' — neither account was theirs.
Poland's foiled Russian false-flag operation was explicitly compared by Polish intelligence sources to the 1939 Gleiwitz incident — the staged attack Germany used to justify invading Poland.

The Ise Shrine in Japan is ritually demolished and entirely rebuilt every 20 years — a practice the Metabolist architects used as conceptual proof that designed impermanence is compatible with cultural permanence.

Energy-Based Reasoners achieve 99.9% accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme puzzles with only 1.8 million parameters, using 345× less inference compute than the next-best model — by framing reasoning as gradient descent on a learned energy landscape rather than token prediction.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A film-essay that moves between Japan, Guinea-Bissau, and Iceland treating memory as a system — feedback loops of image, ritual, and forgetting. Pure rabbit-hole material: the kind of thing that rewires how you see everything else you make.

art_picks.title: Selected Ambient Works Volume II
art_picks.creator: Aphex Twin
art_picks.why: One of the few records that genuinely functions as a system rather than a sequence — each piece a different texture of time, silence used as structure. Obsessive craft in service of something that resists being named.

art_picks.title: World Receiver / Globus Cassus
art_picks.creator: Christian Waldvogel
art_picks.why: A project proposing the mathematical inversion of Earth into a hollow sphere — equal parts cosmological thought experiment, architectural drawing, and mythology as systems design. The kind of unreasonably deep single idea that makes you want to go build something.

events.name: Sandra Cinto: The Path to Stars
events.venue: Tanya Bonakdar Gallery, 521 West 21st Street, New York
events.why: Cinto's immersive wall paintings, tondo canvases, and folding screens dissolve the gallery into sky — drawing used as architecture, the boundary between inside space and celestial system made genuinely permeable.

events.name: NYC Jewelry Week 2026 — Slow Matter Exhibition
events.why: Eight artists working in lacquer and stone — materials defined by deep time and repetition — framed as a conversation about process and patience; the kind of obsessive craft with quiet conceptual depth that rarely gets this kind of platform.

events.name: Leonora Carrington & Cecilia Vicuña: An Exhibition of Affinities
events.venue: Lehmann Maupin, 501 West 24th Street, New York
events.why: Two artists whose practices are fundamentally about mythology as lived system — Carrington's surrealist cosmologies in dialogue with Vicuña's new work, a lineage directly handed from one to the other in 1969 and still alive today.

events.name: NYC Jewelry & Antique Object Show (JAOS)
events.venue: Metropolitan Pavilion, 125 W 18th Street, New York
events.why: A tightly curated show of antique and contemporary jewelry, vintage watches, and exceptional objects — the kind of event where the strange history of ordinary things and the hidden systems of collecting and status are right on the surface.

events.name: artport: A History of Internet Art
events.venue: Whitney Museum of American Art, 99 Gansevoort Street, New York
events.why: The Whitney's 25-year survey of net art commissions — presented simultaneously online and in-gallery with an open floor plan designed to evoke floating browser windows — is a direct hit on the physical/digital edge and the history of software as self-expression.
